title: Architecture
description: Deep Sharp Runtime architecture: native execution, namespaces, physical components, CMake ownership, dependency closure, resources, platforms, exceptions, and tests.
lead: How a familiar System.* surface becomes a selective, boundary-validated set of native C++23 components.

title: Runtime Overview
description: A technical tour of Sharp Runtime subsystem families, native representations, component boundaries, dependencies, and verification evidence.
lead: Understand the complete runtime from core native representations through collections, data, I/O, networking, concurrency, and platform services.

title: Type System
description: Sharp Runtime primitive aliases, native values, Object, Type, strings, arrays, spans, nullable, enums, boxing limits, casts, equality, and ownership.
lead: Use familiar type landmarks without mistaking native C++ values, ownership, RTTI, and templates for a CLR type system.

title: Strings and Text
description: Sharp Runtime string layers, UTF-8 byte semantics, System::String helpers, StringBuilder, encodings, comparisons, and Unicode boundaries.
lead: Choose the right layer for native UTF-8 values, familiar String algorithms, incremental construction, and explicit encoding conversion.

title: System::String Helpers
description: Deep System::String reference for construction model, search, comparison, split, formatting, trimming, conversion, hashing, culture, and .NET deviations.
lead: A practical behavioral reference for the static String algorithms over Sharp Runtime’s native UTF-8 std::string representation.

title: System::Array Helpers
description: Source-verified System::Array algorithms over std::vector: sorting, copying, searching, validation, ownership, invalidation, exceptions, and .NET differences.
lead: Use familiar array algorithms without mistaking a static native helper for the CLR array object model.

title: System::Nullable<T>
description: Source-verified Nullable<T> value semantics, access, equality, NaN behavior, hashing, conversion, ownership, exceptions, and C# differences.
lead: Represent optional values with native construction and equality rules, without confusing absence with pointer ownership.

title: System::EventHandler<TEventArgs>
description: Source-verified EventHandler subscriptions, removal tokens, snapshot dispatch, replay hooks, exceptions, thread safety, lifetime, and .NET differences.
lead: Understand the native type that deliberately combines a callback signature with event subscription and dispatch storage.

title: String Internals
description: Sharp Runtime string representation, UTF-8 units, ownership, lifetime, comparison, hashing, formatting, StringBuilder, encodings, and native interop.
lead: How native byte storage shapes the lifetime, mutation, Unicode, culture, formatting, and interop behavior behind familiar string APIs.

title: Arrays, Spans, and Memory
description: Choose Sharp Runtime owned sequences, Array algorithms, Span, Memory, ArraySegment, and collection representations with explicit lifetime rules.
lead: Separate ownership, algorithms, and borrowed contiguous views before translating C# array code.

title: Array Internals
description: Deep Sharp Runtime array internals: vectors, System::Array, spans, memory, segments, bounds, overlap, ownership, invalidation, and multidimensional choices.
lead: Understand the storage, range validation, copying, invalidation, and lifetime contracts behind every Sharp Runtime array-shaped representation.

title: I/O, Files, and Streams
description: Architecture, ownership, component boundaries, error contracts, and platform behavior across Sharp Runtime’s System.IO implementation.
lead: A code-first guide to streams, files, directories, readers, writers, watchers, compression, hashing, and storage.

title: Threading, Tasks, Channels, and Timers
description: Deep source-backed guide to Sharp Runtime thread lifecycle, synchronization, cancellation, task scheduling, channel backpressure, timers, and native lifetime boundaries.
lead: Understand how familiar System.Threading APIs map to native threads, eager tasks, blocking channels, and timer callbacks.

title: Streams, Readers, and Writers
description: Deep reference for Sharp Runtime Stream capabilities, concrete streams, binary formats, text encoding, ownership, and close behavior.
lead: Understand byte transfer, capabilities, buffering, reader/writer protocols, and native lifetime before porting System.IO code.

title: Files, Directories, Paths, and Metadata
description: Sharp Runtime filesystem semantics for File, Directory, Path, FileInfo, DirectoryInfo, FileStream, RandomAccess, and DriveInfo.
lead: Use native filesystem APIs precisely, with explicit path, metadata, error, portability, and lifetime boundaries.

title: FileSystemWatcher
description: Linux inotify event semantics, live reconfiguration, callback threading, self-stop repair, and current Sharp Runtime watcher limits.
lead: A precise guide to what the watcher delivers, how it rearms and stops, and where the Linux backend remains intentionally partial.

title: Platforms and Portability
description: Evidence-driven platform and subsystem matrix for Linux, Windows, macOS, Emscripten, and Android at the pinned Sharp Runtime revision.
lead: Separate source paths, cross-builds, native runtime evidence, and full test gates before making deployment claims.

title: Known Limitations
description: Current non-goals, reduced semantics, platform limits, lifetime hazards, and verification conditions at the pinned Sharp Runtime source.
lead: An implementation-backed boundary map for deciding what Sharp Runtime can safely replace in a native C++ port.

title: Porting C# Code
description: Flagship guide to porting C# classes, types, properties, arrays, collections, strings, events, tasks, I/O, networking, JSON, XML, and ownership to Sharp Runtime C++.
lead: Translate observable behavior and managed lifetime assumptions into explicit, tested native C++23 design.

title: Adding Runtime Features
description: Contributor workflow for selecting component ownership, implementing APIs, registering CMake, testing behavior and negative consumers, validating boundaries, and regenerating documentation.
lead: Add the smallest correct compatibility slice while preserving native ownership, graph visibility, platform honesty, and reproducible evidence.

title: Tutorials
description: Task-oriented Sharp Runtime tutorials for consumers, C# ports, I/O, networking, concurrency, and contributors, with explicit components and verification status.
lead: Build working native programs, port managed patterns deliberately, and contribute verified runtime behavior.

title: Use Nullable Values
description: Represent present and absent values with Sharp Runtime Nullable, choose fallbacks, and distinguish optional values from pointer ownership.
lead: Preserve absence as data without allocating an object or inventing a sentinel.

title: Work with Arrays and Spans
description: Own native sequences, create checked borrowed spans, copy overlapping ranges, and avoid view invalidation in Sharp Runtime.
lead: Separate owned vectors from borrowed contiguous views before translating array operations.

title: Round-trip Data with MemoryStream
description: Write and read a binary record through Sharp Runtime MemoryStream with explicit position, encoding, and leave-open ownership.
lead: Build a small in-memory binary protocol while preserving stream and wrapper lifetimes.

title: Use Readers and Writers
description: Choose Sharp Runtime binary or text reader/writer stacks with precise byte order, encoding, buffering, close, and ownership contracts.
lead: Select a byte protocol or text policy deliberately instead of relying on familiar .NET type names.

title: Watch a Directory
description: Configure Sharp Runtime FileSystemWatcher on Linux, handle callback reconfiguration safely, reconcile events, and stop without self-join hazards.
lead: Treat inotify events as change hints and design callback, reconfiguration, and teardown boundaries explicitly.

title: Use DNS, TCP, and UDP
description: Resolve hosts and use Sharp Runtime TCP and UDP clients with explicit address families, socket ownership, errors, and platform evidence.
lead: Move from name resolution to an owned native transport without hiding IPv4, lifetime, or blocking behavior.

title: Use WebSockets
description: Connect, send, receive, fragment, and close with Sharp Runtime ClientWebSocket while preserving async buffer and object lifetimes.
lead: Use the RFC 6455 client honestly: ws:// only, borrowed asynchronous buffers, and explicit task completion.

title: Use Locks and ThreadPool
description: Apply RAII to Sharp Runtime Monitor locks and queue work with honest detached-thread, exception, capture, and Emscripten behavior.
lead: Preserve monitor semantics without losing C++ cleanup and callback lifetime safety.

title: Build a Channel Pipeline
description: Use bounded, unbounded, and priority Sharp Runtime channels with backpressure, completion, shared endpoint lifetime, and safe payload ownership.
lead: Connect producers and consumers with an explicit capacity, completion protocol, and native message lifetime.

title: Use Timers Safely
description: Choose Sharp Runtime threading or event timers and manage dedicated threads, callbacks, rescheduling, exceptions, and teardown hazards.
lead: Schedule native callbacks without mistaking stop or dispose for an in-flight completion barrier.

title: Write a Component Test
description: Add a Sharp Runtime GoogleTest to the owning component, cover behavioral boundaries, build it serially, and distinguish discovery from execution.
lead: Turn one public compatibility claim into focused, discoverable, source-owned evidence.

title: Add a Negative Consumer Fixture
description: Prove forbidden Sharp Runtime consumer code remains rejected using clean baselines, isolated negative sites, diagnostic fragments, and component-derived includes.
lead: Make a compile-time boundary failure specific, reproducible, and impossible to pass for an unrelated reason.
